## 2024-05-01 - [DOM XSS in HtmlWebpackPlugin Template]
**Vulnerability:** The `index.html` template generated by `HtmlWebpackPlugin` in `webpack.config.js` blindly reflected the `widgetName` query parameter into the DOM using `document.body.innerHTML += "..."` when the widget ID was omitted, or dynamically injected it as a `<script>` `src` without validation. This allowed arbitrary JavaScript execution (DOM-based XSS) via manipulating the URL (e.g., `?widgetName=<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>`).
**Learning:** Build-time templates that embed runtime values (like URL search parameters) must be treated as untrusted inputs. Using `innerHTML` with unsanitized parameters directly introduces XSS. Furthermore, dynamically loading scripts based on URL parameters without a strict allowlist can lead to script injection.
**Prevention:**
1. Avoid `innerHTML` whenever possible. Use `textContent` for text insertion to ensure it is rendered as text and not evaluated as HTML.
2. Maintain a strict allowlist of known-good values at build-time (e.g., derived from filesystem `glob` results). Validate untrusted inputs (like query parameters) against this allowlist before acting on them, especially before dynamically generating `<script>` elements.
